components.name: machine
components.description: Token machine followed by a host name, or the token default which matches any host.

components.name: login
components.description: Token login followed by a user name.

components.name: password
components.description: Token password followed by an unquoted string with no spaces, or a double-quoted string (curl 7.84.0 and later).

claims.statement: In curl's .netrc handling an entry is a machine (or default) token followed by login and password tokens; each field is a sequence of characters ending with a space or newline, so an entry may span lines or sit on one line.

sources.supports: The .netrc file format is simple: you specify lines with a machine name and follow that with the login and password that are associated with that machine. Each field is provided as a sequence of letters that ends with a space or newline. ... It can also be written on a single line with the same functionality.

claims.statement: Since curl 7.84.0 quoted strings (double quotes with escapes for the quote, newline, carriage return and tab) are supported, and quoting is the only way a space can appear in a username or password.

sources.supports: Since 7.84.0, curl also supports quoted strings. They start and end with double quotes and support the escaped special letters. Quoted strings are the only way a space character can be used in a username or password.

claims.statement: curl's page tells the reader that when a password token is present the file should not be readable by anyone besides the user; the password token is optional.

sources.supports: Supply a password. If this token is present, curl supplies the specified string if the remote server requires a password as part of the login process. Note that if this token is present in the .netrc file you really should make sure the file is not readable by anyone besides the user.

claims.statement: default matches any machine name, there can be only one and it must come after all machine tokens; macdef defines a macro, which curl does not support and skips without affecting the rest of the file.

sources.supports: default ... matches any name. There can be only one default token, and it must be after all machine tokens. macdef name: Define a macro. This is not supported by curl. In order for the rest of the .netrc to still work fine, curl properly skips every definition done with macdef that it finds.

claims.statement: The page calls login the username string and gives "default login anonymous password user@domain" as a default anonymous login; it does not say whether a login value is confidential or whether the anonymous password is a placeholder rather than a secret.

sources.supports: login name: The username string for the remote machine. ... To provide a default anonymous login for hosts that are not otherwise matched, add a line similar to this in the end: default login anonymous password user@domain

claims.statement: No specification shared by all .netrc readers (ftp clients, curl, other libraries) was read. Behaviour outside curl, including the account token, is not asserted.

sources.supports: The page describes curl's support for the format that ftp clients have supported for decades; it is not a specification of the format.

notes: Project-authored by the Redact Secret project, which maintains this repository; not independent evidence. Draft; not yet reviewed.
